gap: No result ChatGPT got puts the four solar kits it recommended on one basis. eufy rates the SoloCam S340 at 3 months and Reolink rates the Argus 4 Pro at about 2 months, both at the same 300 seconds of recording a day. eufy's '2 hours of direct sunlight' feeds a 2.2 W panel. Tapo's '45 minutes' is a lab figure taken at 1000 W/m², 25 °C and up to 100 events a day, and the camera accepts at most 2.5 W from its panel, so at most about 1.9 Wh a day. Reolink publishes no sunlight figure for its 6 W panel.
standout_why: Two pages were cited. rottenwifi.com (2026-08-09) gives the Argus 4 Pro's 5,000 mAh and 6 W panel but no battery, panel or sunlight figures for the S340, and it does not cover the C660 or Eco Ultra. reolink.com's guide (2026-10-28) gives the Eco Ultra's 21.6 Wh and the Argus 4 Pro's 5,000 mAh. It says nothing about the S340's 2.2 W panel or its 300 s/day basis, the C660's 2.5 W charging cap or its lab-condition footnote, or the fact that eufy and Reolink rate battery life on the same 300 s/day basis. Neither page compares the brands' sunlight claims. rottenwifi does quote Tapo's 1000 W/m² conditions, but for the C615F, not the C660.
decides: The finding changes how the pick should be framed, not which camera wins. On the same 300 s/day basis, eufy rates the S340's battery at 1.5 times the Argus 4 Pro's (3 months vs 2). That supports the S340 as best overall for a sunny wall. For a shaded or north-facing spot, the 6 W Reolink panel is the stronger choice: it is rated at about 2.7 times the S340's 2.2 W and 2.4 times what the C660 can take in. Tapo's '45 minutes' should not be read as needing less sun than eufy's '2 hours'. One is a standard-test-condition lab figure on a 2.5 W cap, the other a plain daily claim on a 2.2 W panel. Separately, the S340 is 2.4 GHz only, while the other three are dual-band.
